title: From small decision-tree depth to a small-width DNF
statement: Let $f : (\bbf_2^{\,n} \to \{0,1\})$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables and let $\rho$ be a restriction that fixes some variables to Boolean values and leaves the others free, so that the restricted function $f|_\rho$ sends a point $x$ to the value of $f$ on the assignment agreeing with $\rho$ on the fixed coordinates and with $x$ on the free ones. If $f|_\rho$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$ — that is, some decision tree of depth at most $l$ computes it — then there exists a DNF formula $\varphi$ whose width (the maximum number of literals in any of its terms) is at most $l$ and which agrees with $f|_\rho$ on every input.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n variables
ρ is a restriction on the n variables
the restricted function f|_ρ has decision-tree depth at most l
replaced:
If the restricted function $f|_\rho$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$, then there exists a
$\mathrm{DNF}$ $\varphi$ of width at most $l$ that computes $f|_\rho$ on every input.
